extracted.intended_audience: writers seeking literary representation (authors querying Westwood Creative Artists)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and sending a query/submission to Westwood Creative Artists, including required materials, formatting, agent-selection rules, and response expectations. Targets authors of fiction, narrative nonfiction, and illustrated/graphic projects seeking representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credentials / bio and contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: your credentials/bio and contact information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a short author bio and clear contact details so the agency can follow up. Listed as a required component of the query package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant social media handles
rubrics_metrics.description: any relevant social media handles
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include social media accounts that demonstrate public engagement or readership; the agency notes demonstrated ability to connect with readers is valued by publishers and therefore by them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief synopsis of your work
rubrics_metrics.description: a brief synopsis of your work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise summary of the project being queried so agents can quickly understand premise, stakes, and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing sample: length and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: a writing sample of ten to twenty pages, sent within the body of the email (not as an attachment, please!)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit 10–20 pages only; paste the sample directly into the email body rather than attaching files. This is an explicit formatting/acceptance rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior submission history
rubrics_metrics.description: prior submission history for the project
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose whether and where the project has been submitted previously; helps agents assess rights/status and prior editorial response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art sample for graphic/illustrated projects
rubrics_metrics.description: for graphic or illustrated projects, please also provide an art sample if one is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include representative artwork for illustrated/graphic novels alongside the writing sample when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer to Chicago Manual of Style for formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are unsure about formatting, please refer to the Chicago Manual of Style guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard professional book-manuscript conventions; follow Chicago style when in doubt about punctuation, citation, and formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarize yourself with individual agents' interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Our agents bring their unique interests to their individual client lists, and we encourage you to familiarize yourself with what each of us is prioritizing when it comes to new submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read agent bios and recent client lists to target the agent whose tastes and current priorities align with your project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired author qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally speaking, we are looking for authors who have a mastery of language, a passionate, expert or original perspective on their subject, and a gift for storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should demonstrate strong craft (sentence-level skill), distinct/expert viewpoint, and compelling narrative ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welcoming diverse and underrepresented perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: We very much welcome submissions from authors from diverse backgrounds and from prospective clients whose perspectives have traditionally been underrepresented in publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency explicitly encourages queries from diverse and underrepresented writers; this is a positive selection criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated ability to connect with readers is valued
rubrics_metrics.description: Though it isn’t strictly necessary, a demonstrated ability to connect with readers, whether by social media platform or other means, is greatly valued by publishers, and therefore by us as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform-building (readership, community engagement) strengthens a submission but is not mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of works WCA represents
rubrics_metrics.description: WCA represents: literary, upmarket, and quality commercial fiction in all age categories; a wide range of narrative non-fiction; a limited range of practical non-fiction, including cookbooks and wellness titles; select graphic novels and other illustrated works with high quality writing for all age categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit only projects that fit these categories; the agency is selective about genres and commercial positioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions: not represented
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note that WCA does not represent screenwriters, playwrights or poets, and that we are proud to specialize in representing Canadian authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit scripts, plays, or poetry. Preference/strength for Canadian authors is noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to send queries
rubrics_metrics.description: Send all queries to: submissions@wcaltd.com
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions must be sent to this central email address; the agency only accepts electronic submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submissions only
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note that we only accept electronic submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical mail or other non-electronic formats will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include agent name in subject if appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: If you believe your query is best suited for a particular agent please include their name in the subject line of your email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If targeting an agent by taste/roster, name them in subject to route the query; still obey the rule not to query multiple agents simultaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not query more than one agent simultaneously
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not query more than one agent at the agency simultaneously
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only send a query to one agent at Westwood at a time to avoid internal conflicts and respect agency processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit only one work at a time
rubrics_metrics.description: please only submit one work at a time (until we have had a chance to review and respond to your first query).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send multiple different projects concurrently; wait for the agency to respond before querying additional works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Some agents are closed or by-referral only
rubrics_metrics.description: The following agents are closed to submissions: Briar Heckman, Sara Harowitz, Geffen Semach, and Meg Wheeler. The following agents are closed to submissions except by referral: Jackie Kaiser, Michael Levine, Hilary McMahon, and John Pearce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check agent availability before targeting them; if closed, do not query them unless you have a referral where specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated receipt and selective reply policy
rubrics_metrics.description: You will receive an automated response when your query has been received in our system. Because we receive an extremely high volume of submissions daily, we regret that we are only able to reply to successful queries at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect an auto-confirmation but not a rejection notice; lack of reply does not mean your query was not received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow up to six months for consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Please allow up to six months for our team to consider your submission. If we have not replied within that time, it can be assumed that for one reason or another we have decided against pursuing the project, and we wish you the best in finding alternative representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not follow up repeatedly before six months; absence of reply after six months should be taken as a rejection.
